Dad teaches that volunteering in church is a key way to participate and serve God.

Here's what he said about it:
*   In "FAQs," Dad encourages volunteering in church for special events, like one for kids on May 27. He explains that engaging in tasks together, such as volunteering, builds bonds and strengthens relationships [2][4].
*   In "Day 23," Dad emphasizes the importance of being involved in the service of God in the local church, by being part of a team or department and serving wholeheartedly. He states that part of service is making yourself available to be trained [3].
*   In "Prayer Works," Dad shared his own testimony of volunteering in his family church by learning to play the keyboard, becoming useful, and serving in the choir. He realized that as he gave himself to his own development, he didn't need to fight for places in the church because they found him useful and an asset [6][9].
*   In "The Power of the Spirit 3 - 2nd Service," Dad explains that serving is not about coming to do only what you are good at, but being available for whatever is needed, even if you need to be taught. He stresses that Christians come to church to be blessed *and* to serve one another, such as by cleaning chairs or teaching God's word [12].
*   In "Vision Sunday 2026," Dad says that if God will do anything on earth, He will use people, so you might as well volunteer yourself to be a channel for God through action [13].
*   In "HCM 2025," Dad instructs believers not to be "paralyzed parts" of the church, but to be active. This includes joining the church in giving, building, going on visitation, and soul-winning, asking yourself what the church is doing that you haven't started doing yet [14].

However, Dad does mention that he was taught good traditions from home about attending church regularly, even before he was a pastor [14]. He also teaches about the importance of house churches:
*   In **40 Dot Immersion**, Dad explains that when you go to a new place, you can start by live-streaming, inviting people for a watch party, and from there it becomes a cell or a house church. He mentions that two people are enough to build a gathering [1].
*   In **HCM 2025**, Dad says that a house church starts with as few as two or three people. He shares how he started this church by looking for converts and preaching together with them [16]. He also describes a strategy where someone moves into a neighborhood, forms connections, and a house church starts before they know it, similar to how the early church spread [4].
*   In **Wonders of Personal Fellowship**, Dad states that the goal for members in the diaspora is to grow to the point where they can start a house church, defining it as calling people to join you, even just two or three. He notes that many early churches of the apostles started in people's houses [6].
*   In **Day 40 - Morning Session**, Dad encourages members in the diaspora, whose churches might be meeting in house churches, to check on their invitees and perfect arrangements for transportation to gather people [13].

turns.answer:
Overcoming fear and anxiety involves understanding their nature, recognizing God's provision against them, and actively engaging in spiritual practices to counter them.

Dad teaches that anxiety is a manifestation of fear, and worry is a disturbing, scary, fearful thought about tomorrow [2]. Fear is an enemy of a sound mind, making people irrational [3]. Our Senior Pastor adds that fear is not just a feeling but a tormenting spirit that paralyzes and hinders progress [6]. Dad likens fear to cancer, explaining that it spreads if not cut off immediately [10]. Many fears, such as the fear of flying, are ultimately rooted in the fear of death, and psychologists even say most fears are irrational because they will never happen [13][16]. Fear in one area can also open up other areas of your life to the enemy [18].

To overcome fear and anxiety, several key principles are shared:

1.  **Understand God's provision against fear:**
    *   **God has not given us a spirit of fear:** Dad emphasizes that God has given us a spirit of love, power, and a sound mind, not fear (2 Timothy 1:6) [3]. Our Senior Pastor echoes this, stating that God has not given us the spirit of fear or timidity [6]. We have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear (Romans 8:15) [3].
    *   **The love of God casts out all fear:** Fear is bondage, but God's love, which is already in our hearts, casts it out [3]. The presence of God, specifically His love for us, is the antidote to fear [11][17]. He is with us with good intentions and has the capacity to protect us [17].
    *   **God delivers from all fears:** David sought the Lord and was delivered from all his fears, and Dad teaches that if God heard David, He will hear us too [6][18].
    *   **Don't worry, trust God:** Dad explains that "take no thought" means "don't worry about it" (Matthew 6:25) [2][8]. Worry exposes areas of your life to the enemy, as seen with Job, whose fear and anxiety exposed his children and estate (Job 3:25) [8].

2.  **Actively engage in spiritual warfare and apply God's Word:**
    *   **Face your fears:** Champions are those who overcome fears, not those who never had them. You must confront what is dogging you and say "no more" [1]. Dad recalls an experience where he faced a fierce lion in a dream by rebuking it in his spirit, and it "skimped away," signifying the end of that fear [1]. There comes a time you've got to face that thing [1][15].
    *   **Cut it off and repent:** Fear needs to be cut off immediately, like cancer [10]. You can repent of fear, crying out to the Lord like David did in Psalm 34, asking Him to deliver you from all fears [10][18].
    *   **Warfare in your mind:** The mind is where the real battle is. You cannot overcome thoughts with thoughts; you must open your mouth and speak the right thing, pleading the blood of Jesus and harassing the devil back [4].
    *   **Command fear and anxiety:** When incessant fear or anxiety rises, command it in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, saying, "I overcome you. I come against you and I come after you by the power of the Holy Spirit. And I suppress you. I neutralize you now" [7].
    *   **Master the Word on victory over fear:** Dedicate time to studying and meditating on teachings about victory over fear and faith. Gather all scriptures that speak against fear and how a believer overcomes it [5].
    *   **Seek solitude:** Withdrawing from distractions, people, and social media can help you miss anxiety and fear, along with other negative influences. This helps create space to hear God [9].
    *   **Experience God's peace:** God is quieting every noise of worry, anxiety, and fear, bringing His peace into your heart and mind [14]. This peace that passes all understanding quiets your spirit [14].

Our Senior Pastor teaches that good works are not the price we pay to be saved, but rather they are the proof and result of salvation [3][6][7].

She explains that salvation is a free gift received by grace through faith, and not by works, so that no one can boast (Ephesians 2:8-9) [7][8]. The gospel itself imparts faith for salvation when heard, and this faith is what we use to believe God [12][16]. God is so good and intentional that at the point of salvation, He gave us His own faith to receive it, not asking us to bring our own [1]. Salvation is an expression of God's mercy and has always been His original plan [13][14]. It is for everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord and believes the gospel, regardless of their background or circumstances, because faith in God is an equalizer [17].

Good works are evidence of our salvation and a sign that we have received the divine nature of God [3]. Just as God Himself does good works—creating everything and declaring it "very good"—when we do good works, we are proving that we are like our Father [3]. Forgiving others, being generous, and raising children well are examples of good works [3][5]. Parenting, for instance, is considered a divine assignment and a good work that God expects us to do well, not leaving it to schools or relatives [5].

It is important to understand that good works are the *result* of salvation, not the cause [3][6]. Under the law, people performed good works to be saved or accepted, but as new creations, we do good works *because* we are justified, not to earn God's approval [6]. God has already approved of us, giving us express permission to do His works [6]. Furthermore, good works are the result of God's working in the believer's heart, because people do not naturally do good on their own [6] (Philippians 2:13). Our Senior Pastor emphasizes that we are saved for a purpose, and this purpose was predetermined from the foundations of the world (Ephesians 2:10) [7][11]. Part of these good works includes preaching the gospel, as every believer has been saved to be sent as a preacher of the Word [7][11].

turns.answer:
Our Senior Pastor teaches that discipleship is a serious, scholarly process of instruction and training that enables believers to live out the eternal life they have received in Christ Jesus, fulfilling God's plan for their lives [1].

Discipleship is not just about knowing but about doing, bringing believers to a place of expression where they walk in the reality of what they know, have, and can do [1]. It is crucial because a believer who is not discipled will find it difficult, if not impossible, to fulfill God's plan [1]. Our Senior Pastor emphasizes that nobody can become everything God designed them to be by themselves; they need someone to help, train, and disciple them, like a sheep needs a shepherd [5].

Key aspects of discipleship include:
*   **A Heart for Learning:** It's not a function of age, but a heart that wants to learn, to be equipped, and to grow in understanding and ability [3]. Peter, though older and married, followed Jesus as a student [3].
*   **Following and Learning:** A disciple is a follower who follows hard, desiring to learn and be blessed, equipped, and edified [3]. It involves submitting to a process of discipleship, as Peter did, which helped him become bold, full of faith, and successful [2][5].
*   **Personal Devotion:** Establishing a personal devotion routine, also called quiet time, where you read your Bible and pray every day, is essential for spiritual growth and understanding God's word and ways [2]. Feeding on the word nourishes you with strength, energy, and willpower, just as physical food nourishes the body [10][12].
*   **Spiritual Growth and Service:** The Christian life can be practically frustrating without growth and being of use to the kingdom [18]. Our Senior Pastor encourages believers to take their spiritual growth and service seriously, getting involved in what the church and God are doing, rather than just warming church benches [18].
*   **Structured Avenues for Growth:** The system of discipleship creates avenues and structures for growth, such as small groups, teams for service, and sectors for soul winning [11]. In these small groups, thorough discipleship occurs where leaders can observe and work on believers' character and behavior, helping them live from the inside outwardly [11].
*   **Becoming a Discipler:** Discipleship is a call to faithfulness, where a disciple must pass down exactly what they have been taught, not their own personal opinion [6]. Our Senior Pastor shares that her job is to communicate what Dad has communicated to her, and the goal is for those being taught to also be able to teach others [6][9].

Through discipleship, individuals can grow stronger in spirit, be filled with wisdom for ministry and life, and become effective witnesses of the gospel [4]. It enables believers to stand out, be instruments of increase, and use their faith to address longstanding issues, trusting that God still works with us as we use the faith He has given [13][15][7]. Discipleship puts you ahead in life [3].

turns.answer:
Dad teaches that while the church at Heritage of Faith doesn't necessarily call it tithing, they are not against tithes, and what they practice is called partnership offering [3][6]. This partnership offering is a percentage of your income that you choose to set aside to support the work of the ministry [6].

Here are the key aspects of Dad's teaching on giving and tithing:
*   **Partnership vs. Tithe**: While some churches call it tithe, Dad explains that at Heritage of Faith Church (HHF), it's referred to as partnership offering in line with the New Testament [3][6].
*   **Distinction from Alms Giving**: Giving money to beggars, while honored by God, is called alms giving and is not the same as a tithe or partnership giving, which supports the spread of the gospel of Jesus Christ [1]. Alms giving has its place and is good to help the poor [1].
*   **Recommended Minimum**: Dad encourages believers to give at least 10% of their income, noting that Old Testament believers, who did not have the Holy Ghost, gave 10% [3][6]. He suggests that those in Christ should even do more than that [6].
*   **Free Will**: In the New Testament, giving is an act of free will. While a 10% tithe is basic, you choose the percentage yourself. You can even choose to give less, but it's important to make the right decision [6].
*   **Where to Give**: Your primary place of generosity to the kingdom of God is your local church, where you are spiritually fed [3].
*   **Faithfulness and Capacity**: Your giving should reflect your financial capacity, and it's about being faithful rather than just the amount [10]. Dad notes that the church does not announce big givers because faithfulness is what truly matters [10]. Giving is done as you propose in your heart based on God's blessing in your life [10].
*   **Heart and Commitment**: Giving is a demonstration of the state of your heart and commitment to God's work, the spread of the gospel, and your purpose in Christ Jesus [9][11]. Your treasure indicates where your heart is (Luke 12:34) [11]. When you give, you are giving life because your labor, business, and career involve your life, energy, and time [11].
*   **Expect Returns from God**: When you practice generosity, expect returns from God, not from the people you gave to [4].
*   **Generosity is Not Selective**: Generosity is not selective; if you are truly generous, you will be generous everywhere, not just in church [16].
